messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired — PDQ-4872: prod.inference.p99 > 1.2s (SLO) for /v1/generate. 5m sustained breach in region us-west-1. Current p99: 2.6s. Alert window started ~5m ago. Paging oncall. Link: https://grafana.internal/d/latency/prod?panelId=12

alex: Acked — I'm on the bridge. Starting quick triage. Putting a note in the PD ticket.

incident-bot: alex acknowledged the page (ack at 1767890128). Escalation timer paused.

sam: I see a canary rollback/rollout event around the same time — model-serving/model-v2 canary started ~5:40 UTC. Could be related. deploy link: https://deploys.internal/release/4872

deploy-bot: Canary rollout triggered: model-serving -> model-v2, 10% traffic, started at 2026-03-15T05:40:12Z.

priya: Good catch. Can we check KV cache hit rate and batch size distribution? If model-v2 changed tokenizer or KV layout it could increase cache misses and increase latency. @alex can you pull autoscaler/pod metrics?

alex: Autoscaler shows pods scaled from 12 -> 16 across us-west, but CPU utilization is low (~22%) and queue length/response wait time is up. KV cache eviction rate jumped at the same timestamp as the canary start. Pasting quick tail of kvcache metrics:

```
kvcache.evictions_total{region="us-west-1"}  +1800 (5m)
kvcache.hit_rate{region="us-west-1"} 0.72 -> 0.46
inference.queue_latency_ms.p99 1200 -> 2600
```

alex: No spike in 5xxs in logs. Mostly increased tail latency and some extra queuing.

sam: We should stop the canary (or roll it back) and route traffic back to model-v1 to confirm. I can flip the traffic flag. Command we use: 

```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $FX_TOKEN" \ 
  https://fxflag.internal/api/v1/route \n  -d '{"service":"model-serving","target":"model-v1","weight":100}'
```

alex: Doing traffic flip now. Will monitor.

incident-bot: PagerDuty note: escalation paused by alex at 1767890181.

alex: Traffic flip completed — model-v1 receiving 100% in us-west. Confirming metrics: p99 down to ~1.0s within ~90s. p95 down to ~0.45s.

priya: Nice. That strongly implicates model-v2 path. Any customer-facing impact?

alex: From logs and support queue: ~7% of production requests exceeded p99 during the breach window. No increased 5xxs, but we did see a handful of latency complaints from two larger customers (tickets created). No major error rate increase.

sam: I'll open an incident ticket and attach timeline + Grafana panels. INC-2026-834 created. Adding: canary id 4872, mitigation: traffic reroute to model-v1, observed recovery ~90s post-reroute.

priya: Suggested next steps: 1) Rollback canary fully and hold model-v2 until root cause found. 2) Investigate model-v2 changes: quantization kernels, tokenizer changes, KV cache compatibility. 3) Add canary guardrail: require kvcache hit_rate >= 0.8 during ramp. 4) Add synthetic evals to catch tail regressions before canary.

alex: I've rolled back canary and set model-v2 weight=0. Added an automated alert rule to block canary ramp if kvcache.hit_rate falls >15% from baseline.

maria: Ack — I'm on night oncall handoff in 30m. I'll keep an eye for p99 climbing >1.5s.

alex: Handoff summary for @maria: PDQ-4872 / INC-2026-834 — root cause suspected: model-v2 runtime path causing increased KV cache evictions and queuing, resulting in p99 latency spikes. Mitigation: immediate traffic reroute to model-v1 (done), canary rolled back. Customer impact: transient latency for ~7% requests, minor customer tickets opened. Next owner for postmortem: priya.

maria: Thanks — monitoring set. If p99 > 1.5s for 3 consecutive minutes I'll escalate PD again and ping infra. :thumbsup:

sam: Good catch everyone. We'll schedule a follow-up postmortem and add tighter canary gating. Marking this thread resolved for now — keeping INC-2026-834 open for root-cause work.

incident-bot: Note added to PD incident PDQ-4872: mitigated by traffic reroute; canary rolled back.

alex: Leaving bridge. If anyone sees recurrence ping here or call PD on-call. :white_check_mark:
